text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - German debt burst higher, setting several new record highs as the dour state of Germany's economy and news the U.S. economy was still growing without inflation sweetened the market's mood. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.63, up 0.44 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended near session lows having set yet another contract high earlier after U.S. PPI data landed surprisingly weak and overseas interest in gilts evaporated. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-14/32, up 04/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French 10-year bond futures powered to new historic highs on the back of a sharp overnight advance in U.S. Treasuries. The March notionnel hit an all-time high of 132.28 in early morning trade before retracing to 132.18. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 132.44, up 0.52 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets held at higher levels helped by reassuring comments from Prime Minister Romano Prodi who said he did not rule out a mini-budget and would still like to bring forward the full 1998 budget. Dealers said firmer German bunds, a steady lira and U.S. PPI inflation data also aided the Italian BTP market. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 131.20, up 0.71 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - The prices of U.S. government securities remained well bid at midday as volume began to fall off prior to the close of Friday's abbreviated session. Most dealers seemed content to hold on to gains made earlier in the session on the backs of inflation-friendly producer price and industrial production data. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 113-28/32, up 17/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.54 percent.

JAPAN - Benchmark March Japanese government bond futures ended at the days low, pressured by book-squaring sales which emerged just before the close. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.23, down 0.09 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw an uneventful early session, with marks seeing the most activity and reports of possible further issues from Eastern Europe. Allgemeine Hypothekenbank raised 1.0 billion marks at eight years, Kreditanstalt Fuer Weideraufbau borrowed 500 million marks at a December 2003 maturity and the EIB set a 125 million mark structured five-year FRN. First Austria increased its 10-year bond to 200 million marks.
